$comment: GENERATED-ALIGNED from the DS4AI reference manifest (ds4ai/standards/missing/manifest.json) to the shared standards-family-manifest shape. The DS4AI-specific structure (axes, surfaces, primitives, conformance model) is preserved under `domain`. Members are the nine standards at Polymathie-Studio/ds4ai/standards/<name>. Statuses are honest to the source: seven published, hasp partial (hasp-guard in progress), tuned candidate.
name: DS4AI
author: Regis Lloyd Chapman
description: DS4AI, the Design Suite for AI, from Polymathie-Studio: a family of small, dependency-free primitives for building websites, dashboards, and tools, each closing one invisible-correctness gap that fast, AI-assisted building drops. Native-first, accessible by default, no tracking.

baseline: DS4AI conformance runs through the MISSING auditor (conformance.js) checking a surface against the axes, not through per-instrument schemas.

domain.suite: DS4AI, the Design Suite for AI

jsr.note: Deno-run ES/TS source, no build, mirroring the @proof-of-coord standards servers on JSR. Scope to confirm.

cdn.note: Available for each package once it is on npm; no separate publish.

claudeMarketplace.note: A Polymathie plugin (the agent-instruction plus the conformance checks) via a .claude-plugin marketplace, the way p4ai/pt4ai ships.

mcp.note: A cumulative MCP server for the whole suite, once every primitive is done. Out of scope for this pass.

designTokens.note: TEMPER tokens; W3C DTCG alignment to be decided so they can travel to Figma, Style Dictionary, and Tokens Studio.

agentConfig.note: AGENTS.md ships in the MISSING repo and doubles as the other agent configs; distinct variant files are a later packaging step.

frameworkBindings.note: Every primitive ships a framework-agnostic core plus a React binding today.

conformanceModel.$comment: How a surface conforms and how well the claim is backed. Two questions held apart: breadth (are all six axes closed) and evidence (how the claim was checked). Prose in section 4 of 'MISSING - the standard.md'.

breadthDesignation.name: MISSING Conformant
breadthDesignation.earnedWhen: The surface discharges all six axes.
breadthDesignation.note: A property of the surface, not of any one tool. Carried at whatever evidence level below.

reach.$comment: Reach sets the embodiment of each axis's check, not a separate grade: machine where a check runs against the served HTML, a defined human procedure where it cannot. Both report onto the internal evidence ladder.
reachableFromServedHtml: hardened (markup-integrity and secrets altitude; the header altitude needs the response, declared not-checked when headers are absent)
needsResolvedColors: perceivable (contrast verified against the palette with TEMPER contrast(), not from a snapshot)
needsSurfaceDriven: off-the-happy-path (loading, empty, error, not-found confirmed by driving the surface into each state)

internalEvidenceLadder.$comment: Grades how a conformance claim is backed. Cumulative and nested; describes how the owner checked, never whether the result is good or safe. Ceiling is internal (self-audited, never independent). Words are bare when general to any axis, HASP-prefixed when scoped to the hardening claim (e.g. HASP-audited).

rungs.meaning: A bare claim; the owner says the surface closes the axis.
The claim exposed to a defined, repeatable check anyone could re-apply: the runnable auditor for a machine-reachable axis, the stated procedure for one that is not.
That check actually applied to the surface, and passed. Run-and-re-runnable where the check is a tool, not a snapshot that goes stale.

internalEvidenceLadder.ciNote: A conformance.js run in CI earns audited on the machine-reachable axes and leaves the rest at self-reported until their procedures are applied. MISSING Conformant at the audited level is reached when every axis's defined check has been applied and passed, machine and human procedure together.

reservedExternalLadder.$comment: Held until an independent assessment ecosystem exists; shipping it now would name reviewers who are not in the room. Grades the independence of an assessment, not whether the thing is safe. HASP-prefixed when scoped to the hardening claim.

rules: Never call a surface secure. Describe the territory as client-surface security; grade the measures as hardening and the claim by evidence now or provenance later.
Describe, do not rank: the rungs say how a claim was checked, never that the outcome is good, safe, or correct.
An axis passes when its findings contain no error; an axis marked partial or not-checked is declared, never counted as clean.

conformanceBaseline: Theme via TEMPER tokens with fallbacks
Licensing and family hygiene (Apache-2.0, NOTICE, README family section, CHANGELOG)
notClosedByPrimitive: Observability (error tracking, uptime, performance monitoring): ops-shaped, not a client component.
Backend security and scale (row-level security, connection pooling, token refresh, secrets server-side): out of a frontend family's reach.
Responsive layout: a design-specific discipline, stated as a requirement with no primitive.
Legal content (privacy policy, cookie consent): jurisdiction-specific; tracking is ruled out family-wide.

Delivery transforms and enforcement (image compression, JavaScript bundling, setting cache headers or CDN behavior): build-tool and server work; FLEET emits the markup and config that point at the built assets and audits the result, but cannot encode a pixel, bundle a module, or set a header.

members.name: MISSING
members.description: The umbrella standard and conformance auditor: what a finished front end must cover, and an auditor that checks a surface against it.

members.name: TEMPER
members.description: Color solved to contrast floors; perceivable by any reader.

members.name: GRASP
members.description: Keyboard and screen-reader controls; operable by any input or assistive technology.

members.name: LUCID
members.description: Layered disclosure; complexity placed, not hidden.

members.name: GRACE
members.description: Loading, empty, and error states; the interface behaves honestly off the happy path.

members.name: HASP
members.description: The client-surface security posture the browser can enforce: hasp-key (the user's key stays in their browser, published) plus hasp-guard (headers, policy, integrity; in progress).

members.name: BEACON
members.description: Metadata a crawler and a share can read; the page represents itself correctly to machines.

members.name: FLEET
members.description: Delivery tuned to the Core Web Vitals; emits the markup and config and audits the result.

members.name: TUNED
members.description: The words instrument: written to the utterance, not the established default. Flagship, not yet complete.
